pricing_unit.model: API token commitments and enterprise workspace seats
pricing_unit.summary: Revenue combines a committed token budget with seats for the people who use the model day to day.

core_competitive_threats: Multi-model routing that makes switching cheap
cluster_objections: Open-weight models are nearly as good for our workload. Why should we pay your rate card?
Which model version will we be on in twelve months, and who pays for the migration when you retire it?

market_map.competition: Frontier labs compete on model quality, safety and enterprise controls, while open-weight models and multi-model routers push price per token down.

cards.title: Where it sits
cards.body: Foundation model labs sell the models that apps and agents are built on.

cards.title: What the customer pays for
cards.body: Committed token budgets for the API, plus enterprise workspace seats for people who use the model daily.

cards.title: How the money works
cards.body: Every token has a compute cost, so gross margins run near 50 to 60 percent, not the 80 to 90 percent of seat-based SaaS.

cards.title: What threatens the deal
cards.body: Open-weight models commoditizing the workload, and multi-model routing that makes switching cheap.

quiz.prompt: What makes up a foundation model deal?
quiz.why: Revenue combines a committed token budget with seats for daily users.

quiz.prompt: Why do margins run lower than classic SaaS?
options: Every token carries a compute cost
quiz.why: Inference is a variable cost, so each extra token has a price.
Routing layers let buyers move workloads between models easily.
